newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Truck sales in east Europe to rise 33 pct - Scania.
newsitem.headline: Truck sales in east Europe to rise 33 pct - Scania.

text.p: Heavy truck sales in former communist Europe will rise 33 percent to 200,000 units in 2005 from 150,000 units in 1996, Swedish commercial vehicle maker Scania AB said on Tuesday.

"In the past 10 years the region has developed economically so the demand for trucks to support trade has increased," Ken Tarnstrom, Scania's marketing and sales director in the former Soviet Union, told an automotive conference in Moscow.
"In addition, between 1997 and 2000, the heavy trucks sold during the late 1980s, the last period of strong sales in the region's markets, will need to be replaced."
He said the region's key short-term markets were the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Russia, though he added that Russia remained a quiet market.
